question: The Maitrakas of Valabhi were initially the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**subordinates of the Guptas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maitrakas of Valabhi were initially **subordinates of the Gupta Empire**, serving as local governors or feudatories under Gupta administration.
 
• They established **their independence** following the decline of the Gupta Empire in the 6th century CE.
 
• The Maitrakas ruled from their capital at **Valabhi**, located in present-day Gujarat, which became an important center of trade and learning.
 
• Valabhi was known for its **Buddhist monasteries and learning institutions**, drawing scholars and monks from across India.
 
• The Maitrakas played a key role in maintaining regional stability and fostering cultural and economic growth in western India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gupta Empire:**

 
 
• The Gupta Empire (320-550 CE) is often referred to as the **Golden Age of India** due to advancements in science, art, mathematics, and literature.
 
• Feudatories like the Maitrakas initially served under the Guptas, managing smaller regions within the empire.
 
• The decline of Gupta power led to the emergence of several independent regional kingdoms, including the Maitrakas.
 
 
 
• **Valabhi:**
 
 
• Valabhi was a prominent city and the capital of the Maitrakas, located in modern-day Gujarat.
 
• The city was renowned for its **Buddhist universities**, comparable to Nalanda in eastern India.
 
• Valabhi played a significant role in regional trade and cultural exchanges during the Maitraka rule.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism and Trade:**
 
 
• The Maitrakas were patrons of Buddhism and supported the construction of monasteries and educational institutions.
 
• Valabhi became a hub for Buddhist scholars and monks, contributing to the spread of Buddhist teachings.
 
• The kingdom's location along trade routes fostered economic prosperity and cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **Decline:**
 
 
• The Maitrakas ruled until the **8th century CE**, after which they were overpowered by the Arabs and other emerging forces.
 
• Their contributions to culture and education left a lasting legacy in western India.
